answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it earns reputation or joins paid tasks. A Sybil operator must then fund every clone separately, tying up capital that could otherwise support useful work; if an identity is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed. In an orchard of agents, copper-backed deposits could anchor this rule, while an atlas of signed task records helps detect linked abuse. The cost is real, though: honest newcomers also face a capital barrier.
